Formal authority in Balgrim rests with a local governor, confirmed by Kharzun Delve's central government but drawn, by long custom, from the city's own leading families.

Beneath the formal government, a network of informants loyal to a single retired spymaster exercises real influence in Balgrim — acknowledged quietly by everyone who actually has to get business done there.
Day-to-day administration in Balgrim runs through tax-farmers who keep a cut of everything they collect, a system that works well enough in ordinary times but strains badly under any real crisis.

sections.title: Tension
paragraphs: Balgrim's deepest ongoing friction is over control of a trade toll, a dispute that shapes local politics more than any formal law does.

The root of Balgrim's trouble is control of a trade toll, a dispute old enough that most residents have simply learned to live around it.

paragraphs: Balgrim was settled by Dwarf migrants and grew into its current standing as a city on the strength of its trade in gemstones, which remains the backbone of its economy today.
Balgrim was founded by early Dwarf settlers of Kharzun Delve, drawn to the site by exactly the resources that still support the city's trade.
In its history, Balgrim absorbed a wave of refugees who reshaped its culture within two generations, an event still referenced in local memory and civic ritual.
As a result, it is now the region's acknowledged center of learning, a legacy every resident of Balgrim would recognize immediately even if outsiders rarely do.

sections.title: Urban Life
paragraphs: Balzun runs on a warrior caste ranked above artisans and laborers, a structure visible in everything from who sits closest to the reeve at public gatherings to who gets first pick of goods at market.
Status in Balzun runs on a warrior caste ranked above artisans and laborers, a system locals mostly accept as fair and outsiders mostly find baffling.
Balzun's daily rhythm is set by a weekly rest-day observed even by the guard, observed closely enough that a stranger who ignores it draws immediate notice.
Balzun is built from terraced stone built into the hillside, a style shaped directly by Sunkeep Reaches's climate and the materials its Dwarf founders had on hand.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Balzun answers upward to Kharzun Delve, governed by clan-king holds bound by an ancient mutual-defense oath, though in practice its local rulers exercise considerable day-to-day discretion so long as tribute and trade flow as expected.
Formal authority in Balzun rests with a local reeve, confirmed by Kharzun Delve's central government but drawn, by long custom, from the city's own leading families.
Beneath the formal government, an old veterans' league nobody in office will cross exercises real influence in Balzun — acknowledged quietly by everyone who actually has to get business done there.
Day-to-day administration in Balzun runs through clan-appointed reeves who answer to their own elders first, a system that works well enough in ordinary times but strains badly under any real crisis.

sections.title: Tension
paragraphs: Balzun's deepest ongoing friction is over grazing land, a dispute that shapes local politics more than any formal law does.
Tension in Balzun currently sits at a simmer — real, openly discussed, but not yet at open conflict.
The root of Balzun's trouble is grazing land, a dispute old enough that most residents have simply learned to live around it.
Balzun rarely sees real violence over this, but trade disputes have been known to bring things close to a boil, especially during the busy trading season.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Balzun was settled by Dwarf migrants and grew into its current standing as a town on the strength of its trade in deep-mined ore, which remains the backbone of its economy today.
Balzun was founded by early Dwarf settlers of Kharzun Delve, drawn to the site by exactly the resources that still support the city's trade.
In its history, Balzun absorbed a wave of refugees who reshaped its culture within two generations, an event still referenced in local memory and civic ritual.
As a result, its old founding families still hold outsized influence, a legacy every resident of Balzun would recognize immediately even if outsiders rarely do.

Formal authority in Koradin rests with a local reeve, confirmed by Kharzun Delve's central government but drawn, by long custom, from the city's own leading families.
Beneath the formal government, a smugglers' guild that pays off the harbor watch exercises real influence in Koradin — acknowledged quietly by everyone who actually has to get business done there.

Day-to-day administration in Koradin runs through clan-appointed reeves who answer to their own elders first, a system that works well enough in ordinary times but strains badly under any real crisis.

sections.title: Tension
paragraphs: Koradin's deepest ongoing friction is over water rights, a dispute that shapes local politics more than any formal law does.
Tension in Koradin currently sits at a simmer — real, openly discussed, but not yet at open conflict.
The root of Koradin's trouble is water rights, a dispute old enough that most residents have simply learned to live around it.

sections.title: History

Koradin was founded by early Dwarf settlers of Kharzun Delve, drawn to the site by exactly the resources that still support the city's trade.
In its history, Koradin burned once, entirely, and was rebuilt on the same foundations out of stubbornness, an event still referenced in local memory and civic ritual.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Sandmere Shire is governed by elected burgesses who serve fixed short terms, an arrangement that grew directly out of how Halfling settlers on Sunkeep Reaches organized themselves in the generations after the Doubling of Founding. It has held largely unchanged since, adjusted at the margins but never formally overthrown.

Law in Sandmere Shire is set and interpreted by elected burgesses who serve fixed short terms, with each of the nation's four cities left to handle enforcement details locally so long as they don't contradict the nation's core code.

Authority in Sandmere Shire flows downward from elected burgesses who serve fixed short terms to each city's local ruler, who in turn answers for their city's conduct at the nation's periodic councils.

Sandmere Shire relies on city militias for day-to-day order, backed by standing patrols along its more contested borders — a compromise that keeps costs down but leaves remote stretches thinly watched.

sections.title: Identity
paragraphs: Sandmere Shire is a Halfling-majority nation on Sunkeep Reaches, and its laws, holidays, and public architecture all reflect Halfling custom even where other peoples make up a sizable minority of its population.

Sandmere Shire's stated priorities are preserving its autonomy, keeping its trade routes secure, and honoring the Long Peace Accords — though in practice the first two frequently take precedence over the third when they conflict.

Sandmere Shire occupies territory on Sunkeep Reaches that its people have held since before the Long Peace, giving its claim to the land a legitimacy few neighbors formally dispute, whatever they say in private.

Sandmere Shire maintains formal ties with its neighbors on Sunkeep Reaches and trade contacts reaching all three other continents, conducted mostly through its merchant houses rather than formal embassies.

sections.title: Economy
paragraphs: Sandmere Shire's economy runs on caravan trade, spice, and preserved foodstuffs, produced and traded through its four principal cities and shaping nearly every other aspect of its politics, from tax policy to who holds real influence in elected burgesses who serve fixed short terms.

Sandmere Shire produces caravan trade, spice, and preserved foodstuffs in quantities enough to export widely, a trade that has made certain families and guilds within the nation disproportionately wealthy and influential.

Sandmere Shire exports caravan trade, spice, and preserved foodstuffs through its four principal cities, trading them for goods its own land and craft cannot supply — a dependency that keeps its merchant houses politically powerful.

Labor in Sandmere Shire splits between guild-apprenticed craft work in its cities and traditional household or clan labor in its more rural stretches, with real tension between the two systems over status and pay.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Sandmere Shire was founded in the generations following the Doubling of Founding by Halfling settlers on Sunkeep Reaches, consolidating slowly from scattered early settlements into the nation recognized today.

Sandmere Shire's founding myths center on the Doubling of Founding and the nation's first recognized leader, whose exact deeds vary considerably depending on which city's version of the story is being told.
Sandmere Shire consolidated gradually from a scatter of early settlements into its current four principal cities, a process that took generations and was never fully peaceful.

Sandmere Shire's most persistent internal conflict centers on a heretical splinter cult, a dispute old enough that few remember exactly how it started but recent enough that it still shapes local politics.

sections.title: Factions
paragraphs: A faction within Sandmere Shire actively contests water rights, organizing support in whichever of the nation's cities gives it the most leverage.
This faction's central aim is control over a disputed succession, pursued through both legitimate political pressure and, when that fails, quieter means.
Its influence is concentrated in one or two of Sandmere Shire's four cities rather than spread evenly across the nation, which is exactly why the formal government has been slow to move against it.
Elected burgesses who serve fixed short terms remains this faction's chief opponent, treating it as a persistent irritant rather than an existential threat — a judgment that may not age well.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Skyreach Aerie is governed by a sky-monastic order organized around teaching lineages, an arrangement that grew directly out of how Tengu settlers on Sunkeep Reaches organized themselves in the generations after the Doubling of Founding. It has held largely unchanged since, adjusted at the margins but never formally overthrown.

Law in Skyreach Aerie is set and interpreted by a sky-monastic order organized around teaching lineages, with each of the nation's four cities left to handle enforcement details locally so long as they don't contradict the nation's core code.

Authority in Skyreach Aerie flows downward from a sky-monastic order organized around teaching lineages to each city's local ruler, who in turn answers for their city's conduct at the nation's periodic councils.

Skyreach Aerie relies on city militias for day-to-day order, backed by standing patrols along its more contested borders — a compromise that keeps costs down but leaves remote stretches thinly watched.

sections.title: Identity
paragraphs: Skyreach Aerie is a Tengu-majority nation on Sunkeep Reaches, and its laws, holidays, and public architecture all reflect Tengu custom even where other peoples make up a sizable minority of its population.

Skyreach Aerie's stated priorities are preserving its autonomy, keeping its trade routes secure, and honoring the Long Peace Accords — though in practice the first two frequently take precedence over the third when they conflict.

Skyreach Aerie occupies territory on Sunkeep Reaches that its people have held since before the Long Peace, giving its claim to the land a legitimacy few neighbors formally dispute, whatever they say in private.

Skyreach Aerie maintains formal ties with its neighbors on Sunkeep Reaches and trade contacts reaching all three other continents, conducted mostly through its merchant houses rather than formal embassies.

sections.title: Economy
paragraphs: Skyreach Aerie's economy runs on message-relay services and rare inks and pigments, produced and traded through its four principal cities and shaping nearly every other aspect of its politics, from tax policy to who holds real influence in a sky-monastic order organized around teaching lineages.

Skyreach Aerie produces message-relay services and rare inks and pigments in quantities enough to export widely, a trade that has made certain families and guilds within the nation disproportionately wealthy and influential.

Skyreach Aerie exports message-relay services and rare inks and pigments through its four principal cities, trading them for goods its own land and craft cannot supply — a dependency that keeps its merchant houses politically powerful.

Labor in Skyreach Aerie splits between guild-apprenticed craft work in its cities and traditional household or clan labor in its more rural stretches, with real tension between the two systems over status and pay.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Skyreach Aerie was founded in the generations following the Doubling of Founding by Tengu settlers on Sunkeep Reaches, consolidating slowly from scattered early settlements into the nation recognized today.

Skyreach Aerie's founding myths center on the Doubling of Founding and the nation's first recognized leader, whose exact deeds vary considerably depending on which city's version of the story is being told.
Skyreach Aerie consolidated gradually from a scatter of early settlements into its current four principal cities, a process that took generations and was never fully peaceful.

Skyreach Aerie's most persistent internal conflict centers on an old unpaid blood-debt, a dispute old enough that few remember exactly how it started but recent enough that it still shapes local politics.

sections.title: Factions
paragraphs: A faction within Skyreach Aerie actively contests control of a trade toll, organizing support in whichever of the nation's cities gives it the most leverage.
This faction's central aim is control over a heretical splinter cult, pursued through both legitimate political pressure and, when that fails, quieter means.
Its influence is concentrated in one or two of Skyreach Aerie's four cities rather than spread evenly across the nation, which is exactly why the formal government has been slow to move against it.

A sky-monastic order organized around teaching lineages remains this faction's chief opponent, treating it as a persistent irritant rather than an existential threat — a judgment that may not age well.

sections.title: Urban Life
paragraphs: Featherperch runs on a merchant oligarchy that outspends the nobility, a structure visible in everything from who sits closest to the governor at public gatherings to who gets first pick of goods at market.
Status in Featherperch runs on a merchant oligarchy that outspends the nobility, a system locals mostly accept as fair and outsiders mostly find baffling.
Featherperch's daily rhythm is set by a dusk curfew for the unescorted young, observed closely enough that a stranger who ignores it draws immediate notice.
Featherperch is built from salt-washed adobe with flat roofs for drying goods, a style shaped directly by Sunkeep Reaches's climate and the materials its Tengu founders had on hand.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Featherperch answers upward to Skyreach Aerie, governed by a sky-monastic order organized around teaching lineages, though in practice its local rulers exercise considerable day-to-day discretion so long as tribute and trade flow as expected.
Formal authority in Featherperch rests with a local governor, confirmed by Skyreach Aerie's central government but drawn, by long custom, from the city's own leading families.

Beneath the formal government, a moneylenders' circle that outlasts every council election exercises real influence in Featherperch — acknowledged quietly by everyone who actually has to get business done there.

Day-to-day administration in Featherperch runs through a standing bureaucracy inherited from an older empire, a system that works well enough in ordinary times but strains badly under any real crisis.

sections.title: Tension
paragraphs: Featherperch's deepest ongoing friction is over an old unpaid blood-debt, a dispute that shapes local politics more than any formal law does.
Tension in Featherperch currently sits at a simmer — real, openly discussed, but not yet at open conflict.
The root of Featherperch's trouble is an old unpaid blood-debt, a dispute old enough that most residents have simply learned to live around it.
Featherperch rarely sees real violence over this, but trade disputes have been known to bring things close to a boil, especially during the busy trading season.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Featherperch was settled by Tengu migrants and grew into its current standing as a city on the strength of its trade in message-relay services, which remains the backbone of its economy today.
Featherperch was founded by early Tengu settlers of Skyreach Aerie, drawn to the site by exactly the resources that still support the city's trade.
In its history, Featherperch grew rich off a single trade good before diversifying, an event still referenced in local memory and civic ritual.
As a result, outsiders still call it by its older, pre-founding name, a legacy every resident of Featherperch would recognize immediately even if outsiders rarely do.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Undertide Warrens is governed by guild-warrens governed by formal debt-ledger seniority, an arrangement that grew directly out of how Ratfolk settlers on Sunkeep Reaches organized themselves in the generations after the Doubling of Founding. It has held largely unchanged since, adjusted at the margins but never formally overthrown.

Law in Undertide Warrens is set and interpreted by guild-warrens governed by formal debt-ledger seniority, with each of the nation's four cities left to handle enforcement details locally so long as they don't contradict the nation's core code.

Authority in Undertide Warrens flows downward from guild-warrens governed by formal debt-ledger seniority to each city's local ruler, who in turn answers for their city's conduct at the nation's periodic councils.

Undertide Warrens relies on city militias for day-to-day order, backed by standing patrols along its more contested borders — a compromise that keeps costs down but leaves remote stretches thinly watched.

sections.title: Identity
paragraphs: Undertide Warrens is a Ratfolk-majority nation on Sunkeep Reaches, and its laws, holidays, and public architecture all reflect Ratfolk custom even where other peoples make up a sizable minority of its population.

Undertide Warrens's stated priorities are preserving its autonomy, keeping its trade routes secure, and honoring the Long Peace Accords — though in practice the first two frequently take precedence over the third when they conflict.

Undertide Warrens occupies territory on Sunkeep Reaches that its people have held since before the Long Peace, giving its claim to the land a legitimacy few neighbors formally dispute, whatever they say in private.

Undertide Warrens maintains formal ties with its neighbors on Sunkeep Reaches and trade contacts reaching all three other continents, conducted mostly through its merchant houses rather than formal embassies.

sections.title: Economy
paragraphs: Undertide Warrens's economy runs on salvage goods and a well-known black market, produced and traded through its four principal cities and shaping nearly every other aspect of its politics, from tax policy to who holds real influence in guild-warrens governed by formal debt-ledger seniority.

Undertide Warrens produces salvage goods and a well-known black market in quantities enough to export widely, a trade that has made certain families and guilds within the nation disproportionately wealthy and influential.

Undertide Warrens exports salvage goods and a well-known black market through its four principal cities, trading them for goods its own land and craft cannot supply — a dependency that keeps its merchant houses politically powerful.

Labor in Undertide Warrens splits between guild-apprenticed craft work in its cities and traditional household or clan labor in its more rural stretches, with real tension between the two systems over status and pay.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Undertide Warrens was founded in the generations following the Doubling of Founding by Ratfolk settlers on Sunkeep Reaches, consolidating slowly from scattered early settlements into the nation recognized today.

Undertide Warrens's founding myths center on the Doubling of Founding and the nation's first recognized leader, whose exact deeds vary considerably depending on which city's version of the story is being told.
Undertide Warrens consolidated gradually from a scatter of early settlements into its current four principal cities, a process that took generations and was never fully peaceful.

Undertide Warrens's most persistent internal conflict centers on an old unpaid blood-debt, a dispute old enough that few remember exactly how it started but recent enough that it still shapes local politics.

sections.title: Factions
paragraphs: A faction within Undertide Warrens actively contests grazing land, organizing support in whichever of the nation's cities gives it the most leverage.
This faction's central aim is control over a border shrine both sides claim, pursued through both legitimate political pressure and, when that fails, quieter means.

Its influence is concentrated in one or two of Undertide Warrens's four cities rather than spread evenly across the nation, which is exactly why the formal government has been slow to move against it.

Guild-warrens governed by formal debt-ledger seniority remains this faction's chief opponent, treating it as a persistent irritant rather than an existential threat — a judgment that may not age well.

sections.title: Geography
paragraphs: Veyl Isles is defined by coral reef shallows, mangrove wetland, high island canopy forest — a landscape that shaped every nation built on it long before any of their current borders existed. Scattered volcanic islands ringed by reef, dense canopy on the larger islands sets the pattern of where people actually settled, and the climate — tropical, a sharp wet and dry monsoon season — decided what they could grow, mine, or hunt once they did.

The mix of coral reef shallows, mangrove wetland, high island canopy forest on Veyl Isles means no single nation here can rely on one kind of land; every nation's economy blends what each biome offers rather than specializing in just one.

Scattered volcanic islands ringed by reef, dense canopy on the larger islands across Veyl Isles has kept its four nations more separated by geography than by any deliberate border policy — most conflicts here start at a natural chokepoint, not an arbitrary line.

A tropical, a sharp wet and dry monsoon season climate governs the planting, trading, and travel calendar for every nation on Veyl Isles, and every one of them has built its major festivals around it.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Veyl Isles has been settled continuously since before the Doubling of Founding, first by scattered clans of its founding peoples and later by the four organized nations that now hold it. The Veil-Storms of -410 reshaped its coastline and interior alike, and the Long Peace Accords of 112 are still the framework every nation here formally honors, however unevenly.
Histories on Veyl Isles are conventionally divided into the Founding Era (before -410), the unstable Veil-Storm centuries that followed, and the Long Peace that has held, roughly, since 112.
The Veil-Storms remain the single most-referenced disaster in every nation's oldest records on Veyl Isles, blamed for everything from reshaped coastlines to the continent's scattered wild zones.

Population on Veyl Isles has drifted steadily toward its rivers, coasts, and trade roads for generations, hollowing out its more remote interior settlements in favor of its four nations' capitals and market towns.

sections.title: Demographics
paragraphs: Veyl Isles is home to the Catfolk, Grippli, Undine, Vanara peoples, each concentrated in its own nation but present as trading minorities nearly everywhere else on the continent.
Catfolk, Grippli, Undine, Vanara together make up the overwhelming majority of Veyl Isles's population, with small numbers of other Aurvantan peoples present in every major port and market town.
Movement across Veyl Isles runs mostly along its trade roads and river lines rather than across open wilderness, which keeps its nations' borders porous for merchants even when politically tense.
Veyl Isles supports a population in the low millions, weighted heavily toward its four national capitals and the market towns strung along the routes between them.

Vanara craft goods are recognizable across Aurvantis by their distinctive materials and style, and command a premium in foreign markets specifically because of that origin.
Vanara remain most heavily concentrated on Veyl Isles, though small trading communities are found on every other continent as well.

sections.title: Relations
paragraphs: Vanara maintain generally peaceful relations with their neighboring peoples on Veyl Isles, punctuated by periodic disputes over resources or old, specific grievances.
Vanara are represented, unevenly, in the nation of Veyl Isles that shares their cultural roots most closely, and view that nation's government as at least nominally answerable to them.
Vanara maintain both close kin-ties and long-standing rivalries with the other peoples of Veyl Isles, the specifics varying from clan to clan and city to city.
Specific old grievances between Vanara and their neighbors persist in local memory, but rarely rise to open conflict under the terms of the Long Peace.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Kaudrai Canopy is governed by canopy-councils led by the troop's most respected elders, an arrangement that grew directly out of how Vanara settlers on Veyl Isles organized themselves in the generations after the Doubling of Founding. It has held largely unchanged since, adjusted at the margins but never formally overthrown.

Law in Kaudrai Canopy is set and interpreted by canopy-councils led by the troop's most respected elders, with each of the nation's four cities left to handle enforcement details locally so long as they don't contradict the nation's core code.

Authority in Kaudrai Canopy flows downward from canopy-councils led by the troop's most respected elders to each city's local ruler, who in turn answers for their city's conduct at the nation's periodic councils.

Kaudrai Canopy relies on city militias for day-to-day order, backed by standing patrols along its more contested borders — a compromise that keeps costs down but leaves remote stretches thinly watched.

sections.title: Identity
paragraphs: Kaudrai Canopy is a Vanara-majority nation on Veyl Isles, and its laws, holidays, and public architecture all reflect Vanara custom even where other peoples make up a sizable minority of its population.

Kaudrai Canopy's stated priorities are preserving its autonomy, keeping its trade routes secure, and honoring the Long Peace Accords — though in practice the first two frequently take precedence over the third when they conflict.

Kaudrai Canopy occupies territory on Veyl Isles that its people have held since before the Long Peace, giving its claim to the land a legitimacy few neighbors formally dispute, whatever they say in private.

Kaudrai Canopy maintains formal ties with its neighbors on Veyl Isles and trade contacts reaching all three other continents, conducted mostly through its merchant houses rather than formal embassies.

sections.title: Economy
paragraphs: Kaudrai Canopy's economy runs on tropical fruit, rope-fiber, and hardwood, produced and traded through its four principal cities and shaping nearly every other aspect of its politics, from tax policy to who holds real influence in canopy-councils led by the troop's most respected elders.

Kaudrai Canopy produces tropical fruit, rope-fiber, and hardwood in quantities enough to export widely, a trade that has made certain families and guilds within the nation disproportionately wealthy and influential.

Kaudrai Canopy exports tropical fruit, rope-fiber, and hardwood through its four principal cities, trading them for goods its own land and craft cannot supply — a dependency that keeps its merchant houses politically powerful.

Labor in Kaudrai Canopy splits between guild-apprenticed craft work in its cities and traditional household or clan labor in its more rural stretches, with real tension between the two systems over status and pay.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Kaudrai Canopy was founded in the generations following the Doubling of Founding by Vanara settlers on Veyl Isles, consolidating slowly from scattered early settlements into the nation recognized today.

Kaudrai Canopy's founding myths center on the Doubling of Founding and the nation's first recognized leader, whose exact deeds vary considerably depending on which city's version of the story is being told.
Kaudrai Canopy consolidated gradually from a scatter of early settlements into its current four principal cities, a process that took generations and was never fully peaceful.
Kaudrai Canopy's most persistent internal conflict centers on grazing land, a dispute old enough that few remember exactly how it started but recent enough that it still shapes local politics.

sections.title: Factions
paragraphs: A faction within Kaudrai Canopy actively contests an old unpaid blood-debt, organizing support in whichever of the nation's cities gives it the most leverage.
This faction's central aim is control over control of a trade toll, pursued through both legitimate political pressure and, when that fails, quieter means.
Its influence is concentrated in one or two of Kaudrai Canopy's four cities rather than spread evenly across the nation, which is exactly why the formal government has been slow to move against it.

Canopy-councils led by the troop's most respected elders remains this faction's chief opponent, treating it as a persistent irritant rather than an existential threat — a judgment that may not age well.

Status in Leafreach runs on a merchant oligarchy that outspends the nobility, a system locals mostly accept as fair and outsiders mostly find baffling.
Leafreach's daily rhythm is set by ritual bathing before any formal business, observed closely enough that a stranger who ignores it draws immediate notice.
Leafreach is built from salt-washed adobe with flat roofs for drying goods, a style shaped directly by Veyl Isles's climate and the materials its Vanara founders had on hand.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Leafreach answers upward to Kaudrai Canopy, governed by canopy-councils led by the troop's most respected elders, though in practice its local rulers exercise considerable day-to-day discretion so long as tribute and trade flow as expected.
Formal authority in Leafreach rests with a local reeve, confirmed by Kaudrai Canopy's central government but drawn, by long custom, from the city's own leading families.

Beneath the formal government, a moneylenders' circle that outlasts every council election exercises real influence in Leafreach — acknowledged quietly by everyone who actually has to get business done there.
Day-to-day administration in Leafreach runs through rotating magistrates drawn by lot each season, a system that works well enough in ordinary times but strains badly under any real crisis.

sections.title: Tension
paragraphs: Leafreach's deepest ongoing friction is over a heretical splinter cult, a dispute that shapes local politics more than any formal law does.
Tension in Leafreach currently sits at a simmer — real, openly discussed, but not yet at open conflict.
The root of Leafreach's trouble is a heretical splinter cult, a dispute old enough that most residents have simply learned to live around it.
Leafreach rarely sees real violence over this, but trade disputes have been known to bring things close to a boil, especially during the busy trading season.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Leafreach was settled by Vanara migrants and grew into its current standing as a village on the strength of its trade in tropical fruit, which remains the backbone of its economy today.
Leafreach was founded by early Vanara settlers of Kaudrai Canopy, drawn to the site by exactly the resources that still support the city's trade.
In its history, Leafreach was founded explicitly to guard a mountain pass or river ford, an event still referenced in local memory and civic ritual.
As a result, its founding compromise is still cited in local law, a legacy every resident of Leafreach would recognize immediately even if outsiders rarely do.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Mireflote Concord is governed by a wetland concord of allied mire-settlements, an arrangement that grew directly out of how Grippli settlers on Veyl Isles organized themselves in the generations after the Doubling of Founding. It has held largely unchanged since, adjusted at the margins but never formally overthrown.

Law in Mireflote Concord is set and interpreted by a wetland concord of allied mire-settlements, with each of the nation's four cities left to handle enforcement details locally so long as they don't contradict the nation's core code.

Authority in Mireflote Concord flows downward from a wetland concord of allied mire-settlements to each city's local ruler, who in turn answers for their city's conduct at the nation's periodic councils.

Mireflote Concord relies on city militias for day-to-day order, backed by standing patrols along its more contested borders — a compromise that keeps costs down but leaves remote stretches thinly watched.

sections.title: Identity
paragraphs: Mireflote Concord is a Grippli-majority nation on Veyl Isles, and its laws, holidays, and public architecture all reflect Grippli custom even where other peoples make up a sizable minority of its population.

Mireflote Concord's stated priorities are preserving its autonomy, keeping its trade routes secure, and honoring the Long Peace Accords — though in practice the first two frequently take precedence over the third when they conflict.

Mireflote Concord occupies territory on Veyl Isles that its people have held since before the Long Peace, giving its claim to the land a legitimacy few neighbors formally dispute, whatever they say in private.

Mireflote Concord maintains formal ties with its neighbors on Veyl Isles and trade contacts reaching all three other continents, conducted mostly through its merchant houses rather than formal embassies.

sections.title: Economy
paragraphs: Mireflote Concord's economy runs on poisons, dyes, and wetland medicine, produced and traded through its four principal cities and shaping nearly every other aspect of its politics, from tax policy to who holds real influence in a wetland concord of allied mire-settlements.

Mireflote Concord produces poisons, dyes, and wetland medicine in quantities enough to export widely, a trade that has made certain families and guilds within the nation disproportionately wealthy and influential.

Mireflote Concord exports poisons, dyes, and wetland medicine through its four principal cities, trading them for goods its own land and craft cannot supply — a dependency that keeps its merchant houses politically powerful.

Labor in Mireflote Concord splits between guild-apprenticed craft work in its cities and traditional household or clan labor in its more rural stretches, with real tension between the two systems over status and pay.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Mireflote Concord was founded in the generations following the Doubling of Founding by Grippli settlers on Veyl Isles, consolidating slowly from scattered early settlements into the nation recognized today.

Mireflote Concord's founding myths center on the Doubling of Founding and the nation's first recognized leader, whose exact deeds vary considerably depending on which city's version of the story is being told.
Mireflote Concord consolidated gradually from a scatter of early settlements into its current four principal cities, a process that took generations and was never fully peaceful.
Mireflote Concord's most persistent internal conflict centers on smuggling routes, a dispute old enough that few remember exactly how it started but recent enough that it still shapes local politics.

sections.title: Factions
paragraphs: A faction within Mireflote Concord actively contests a disputed succession, organizing support in whichever of the nation's cities gives it the most leverage.
This faction's central aim is control over water rights, pursued through both legitimate political pressure and, when that fails, quieter means.

Its influence is concentrated in one or two of Mireflote Concord's four cities rather than spread evenly across the nation, which is exactly why the formal government has been slow to move against it.
A wetland concord of allied mire-settlements remains this faction's chief opponent, treating it as a persistent irritant rather than an existential threat — a judgment that may not age well.

sections.title: Urban Life
paragraphs: Bogflote runs on a warrior caste ranked above artisans and laborers, a structure visible in everything from who sits closest to the reeve at public gatherings to who gets first pick of goods at market.
Status in Bogflote runs on a warrior caste ranked above artisans and laborers, a system locals mostly accept as fair and outsiders mostly find baffling.
Bogflote's daily rhythm is set by a weekly rest-day observed even by the guard, observed closely enough that a stranger who ignores it draws immediate notice.
Bogflote is built from coral and driftwood stilt-housing, a style shaped directly by Veyl Isles's climate and the materials its Grippli founders had on hand.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Bogflote answers upward to Mireflote Concord, governed by a wetland concord of allied mire-settlements, though in practice its local rulers exercise considerable day-to-day discretion so long as tribute and trade flow as expected.
Formal authority in Bogflote rests with a local reeve, confirmed by Mireflote Concord's central government but drawn, by long custom, from the city's own leading families.
Beneath the formal government, an old veterans' league nobody in office will cross exercises real influence in Bogflote — acknowledged quietly by everyone who actually has to get business done there.

Day-to-day administration in Bogflote runs through clan-appointed reeves who answer to their own elders first, a system that works well enough in ordinary times but strains badly under any real crisis.

sections.title: Tension
paragraphs: Bogflote's deepest ongoing friction is over control of a trade toll, a dispute that shapes local politics more than any formal law does.
Tension in Bogflote currently sits at a simmer — real, openly discussed, but not yet at open conflict.
The root of Bogflote's trouble is control of a trade toll, a dispute old enough that most residents have simply learned to live around it.
Bogflote rarely sees real violence over this, but trade disputes have been known to bring things close to a boil, especially during the busy trading season.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Bogflote was settled by Grippli migrants and grew into its current standing as a town on the strength of its trade in wetland medicine, which remains the backbone of its economy today.
Bogflote was founded by early Grippli settlers of Mireflote Concord, drawn to the site by exactly the resources that still support the city's trade.
In its history, Bogflote split from a larger settlement after a succession dispute, an event still referenced in local memory and civic ritual.
As a result, its old founding families still hold outsized influence, a legacy every resident of Bogflote would recognize immediately even if outsiders rarely do.

sections.title: Urban Life
paragraphs: Sporemarsh runs on a warrior caste ranked above artisans and laborers, a structure visible in everything from who sits closest to the reeve at public gatherings to who gets first pick of goods at market.
Status in Sporemarsh runs on a warrior caste ranked above artisans and laborers, a system locals mostly accept as fair and outsiders mostly find baffling.
Sporemarsh's daily rhythm is set by communal meals at the clan-hall, observed closely enough that a stranger who ignores it draws immediate notice.
Sporemarsh is built from terraced stone built into the hillside, a style shaped directly by Veyl Isles's climate and the materials its Grippli founders had on hand.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Sporemarsh answers upward to Mireflote Concord, governed by a wetland concord of allied mire-settlements, though in practice its local rulers exercise considerable day-to-day discretion so long as tribute and trade flow as expected.
Formal authority in Sporemarsh rests with a local reeve, confirmed by Mireflote Concord's central government but drawn, by long custom, from the city's own leading families.

Beneath the formal government, a network of informants loyal to a single retired spymaster exercises real influence in Sporemarsh — acknowledged quietly by everyone who actually has to get business done there.
Day-to-day administration in Sporemarsh runs through rotating magistrates drawn by lot each season, a system that works well enough in ordinary times but strains badly under any real crisis.

sections.title: Tension
paragraphs: Sporemarsh's deepest ongoing friction is over grazing land, a dispute that shapes local politics more than any formal law does.
Tension in Sporemarsh currently sits at a simmer — real, openly discussed, but not yet at open conflict.
The root of Sporemarsh's trouble is grazing land, a dispute old enough that most residents have simply learned to live around it.
Sporemarsh rarely sees real violence over this, but trade disputes have been known to bring things close to a boil, especially during the busy trading season.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Sporemarsh was settled by Grippli migrants and grew into its current standing as a village on the strength of its trade in poisons, which remains the backbone of its economy today.
Sporemarsh was founded by early Grippli settlers of Mireflote Concord, drawn to the site by exactly the resources that still support the city's trade.
In its history, Sporemarsh absorbed a wave of refugees who reshaped its culture within two generations, an event still referenced in local memory and civic ritual.
As a result, its old founding families still hold outsized influence, a legacy every resident of Sporemarsh would recognize immediately even if outsiders rarely do.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Panthera Reef Courts is governed by a court of clans that meets on neutral reef ground each season, an arrangement that grew directly out of how Catfolk settlers on Veyl Isles organized themselves in the generations after the Doubling of Founding. It has held largely unchanged since, adjusted at the margins but never formally overthrown.

Law in Panthera Reef Courts is set and interpreted by a court of clans that meets on neutral reef ground each season, with each of the nation's four cities left to handle enforcement details locally so long as they don't contradict the nation's core code.

Authority in Panthera Reef Courts flows downward from a court of clans that meets on neutral reef ground each season to each city's local ruler, who in turn answers for their city's conduct at the nation's periodic councils.

Panthera Reef Courts relies on city militias for day-to-day order, backed by standing patrols along its more contested borders — a compromise that keeps costs down but leaves remote stretches thinly watched.

sections.title: Identity
paragraphs: Panthera Reef Courts is a Catfolk-majority nation on Veyl Isles, and its laws, holidays, and public architecture all reflect Catfolk custom even where other peoples make up a sizable minority of its population.

Panthera Reef Courts's stated priorities are preserving its autonomy, keeping its trade routes secure, and honoring the Long Peace Accords — though in practice the first two frequently take precedence over the third when they conflict.

Panthera Reef Courts occupies territory on Veyl Isles that its people have held since before the Long Peace, giving its claim to the land a legitimacy few neighbors formally dispute, whatever they say in private.

Panthera Reef Courts maintains formal ties with its neighbors on Veyl Isles and trade contacts reaching all three other continents, conducted mostly through its merchant houses rather than formal embassies.

sections.title: Economy
paragraphs: Panthera Reef Courts's economy runs on pearls and woven silk, produced and traded through its four principal cities and shaping nearly every other aspect of its politics, from tax policy to who holds real influence in a court of clans that meets on neutral reef ground each season.

Panthera Reef Courts produces pearls and woven silk in quantities enough to export widely, a trade that has made certain families and guilds within the nation disproportionately wealthy and influential.

Panthera Reef Courts exports pearls and woven silk through its four principal cities, trading them for goods its own land and craft cannot supply — a dependency that keeps its merchant houses politically powerful.

Labor in Panthera Reef Courts splits between guild-apprenticed craft work in its cities and traditional household or clan labor in its more rural stretches, with real tension between the two systems over status and pay.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Panthera Reef Courts was founded in the generations following the Doubling of Founding by Catfolk settlers on Veyl Isles, consolidating slowly from scattered early settlements into the nation recognized today.

Panthera Reef Courts's founding myths center on the Doubling of Founding and the nation's first recognized leader, whose exact deeds vary considerably depending on which city's version of the story is being told.
Panthera Reef Courts consolidated gradually from a scatter of early settlements into its current four principal cities, a process that took generations and was never fully peaceful.
Panthera Reef Courts's most persistent internal conflict centers on water rights, a dispute old enough that few remember exactly how it started but recent enough that it still shapes local politics.

sections.title: Factions
paragraphs: A faction within Panthera Reef Courts actively contests a disputed succession, organizing support in whichever of the nation's cities gives it the most leverage.
This faction's central aim is control over smuggling routes, pursued through both legitimate political pressure and, when that fails, quieter means.

Its influence is concentrated in one or two of Panthera Reef Courts's four cities rather than spread evenly across the nation, which is exactly why the formal government has been slow to move against it.

A court of clans that meets on neutral reef ground each season remains this faction's chief opponent, treating it as a persistent irritant rather than an existential threat — a judgment that may not age well.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Tidewrought Commonwealth is governed by a tidal commune that reseats its leadership with the season, an arrangement that grew directly out of how Undine settlers on Veyl Isles organized themselves in the generations after the Doubling of Founding. It has held largely unchanged since, adjusted at the margins but never formally overthrown.

Law in Tidewrought Commonwealth is set and interpreted by a tidal commune that reseats its leadership with the season, with each of the nation's four cities left to handle enforcement details locally so long as they don't contradict the nation's core code.

Authority in Tidewrought Commonwealth flows downward from a tidal commune that reseats its leadership with the season to each city's local ruler, who in turn answers for their city's conduct at the nation's periodic councils.

Tidewrought Commonwealth relies on city militias for day-to-day order, backed by standing patrols along its more contested borders — a compromise that keeps costs down but leaves remote stretches thinly watched.

sections.title: Identity
paragraphs: Tidewrought Commonwealth is a Undine-majority nation on Veyl Isles, and its laws, holidays, and public architecture all reflect Undine custom even where other peoples make up a sizable minority of its population.

Tidewrought Commonwealth's stated priorities are preserving its autonomy, keeping its trade routes secure, and honoring the Long Peace Accords — though in practice the first two frequently take precedence over the third when they conflict.

Tidewrought Commonwealth occupies territory on Veyl Isles that its people have held since before the Long Peace, giving its claim to the land a legitimacy few neighbors formally dispute, whatever they say in private.

Tidewrought Commonwealth maintains formal ties with its neighbors on Veyl Isles and trade contacts reaching all three other continents, conducted mostly through its merchant houses rather than formal embassies.

sections.title: Economy
paragraphs: Tidewrought Commonwealth's economy runs on salt, fish, and worked coral, produced and traded through its four principal cities and shaping nearly every other aspect of its politics, from tax policy to who holds real influence in a tidal commune that reseats its leadership with the season.

Tidewrought Commonwealth produces salt, fish, and worked coral in quantities enough to export widely, a trade that has made certain families and guilds within the nation disproportionately wealthy and influential.

Tidewrought Commonwealth exports salt, fish, and worked coral through its four principal cities, trading them for goods its own land and craft cannot supply — a dependency that keeps its merchant houses politically powerful.

Labor in Tidewrought Commonwealth splits between guild-apprenticed craft work in its cities and traditional household or clan labor in its more rural stretches, with real tension between the two systems over status and pay.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Tidewrought Commonwealth was founded in the generations following the Doubling of Founding by Undine settlers on Veyl Isles, consolidating slowly from scattered early settlements into the nation recognized today.

Tidewrought Commonwealth's founding myths center on the Doubling of Founding and the nation's first recognized leader, whose exact deeds vary considerably depending on which city's version of the story is being told.
Tidewrought Commonwealth consolidated gradually from a scatter of early settlements into its current four principal cities, a process that took generations and was never fully peaceful.

Tidewrought Commonwealth's most persistent internal conflict centers on an old unpaid blood-debt, a dispute old enough that few remember exactly how it started but recent enough that it still shapes local politics.

sections.title: Factions
paragraphs: A faction within Tidewrought Commonwealth actively contests control of a trade toll, organizing support in whichever of the nation's cities gives it the most leverage.
This faction's central aim is control over a heretical splinter cult, pursued through both legitimate political pressure and, when that fails, quieter means.

Its influence is concentrated in one or two of Tidewrought Commonwealth's four cities rather than spread evenly across the nation, which is exactly why the formal government has been slow to move against it.

A tidal commune that reseats its leadership with the season remains this faction's chief opponent, treating it as a persistent irritant rather than an existential threat — a judgment that may not age well.

sections.title: Tension
paragraphs: Deepshoal's deepest ongoing friction is over a border shrine both sides claim, a dispute that shapes local politics more than any formal law does.

The root of Deepshoal's trouble is a border shrine both sides claim, a dispute old enough that most residents have simply learned to live around it.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Deepshoal was settled by Undine migrants and grew into its current standing as a town on the strength of its trade in fish, which remains the backbone of its economy today.
Deepshoal was founded by early Undine settlers of Tidewrought Commonwealth, drawn to the site by exactly the resources that still support the city's trade.
In its history, Deepshoal was founded explicitly to guard a mountain pass or river ford, an event still referenced in local memory and civic ritual.
As a result, its old founding families still hold outsized influence, a legacy every resident of Deepshoal would recognize immediately even if outsiders rarely do.

sections.title: Urban Life
paragraphs: Tidecrest runs on clan seniority set by age and deed, a structure visible in everything from who sits closest to the reeve at public gatherings to who gets first pick of goods at market.
Status in Tidecrest runs on clan seniority set by age and deed, a system locals mostly accept as fair and outsiders mostly find baffling.
Tidecrest's daily rhythm is set by a dusk curfew for the unescorted young, observed closely enough that a stranger who ignores it draws immediate notice.
Tidecrest is built from sunken courtyard houses that trap the cool night air, a style shaped directly by Veyl Isles's climate and the materials its Undine founders had on hand.

sections.title: Governance
paragraphs: Tidecrest answers upward to Tidewrought Commonwealth, governed by a tidal commune that reseats its leadership with the season, though in practice its local rulers exercise considerable day-to-day discretion so long as tribute and trade flow as expected.
Formal authority in Tidecrest rests with a local reeve, confirmed by Tidewrought Commonwealth's central government but drawn, by long custom, from the city's own leading families.

Beneath the formal government, a temple faction that quietly funds half the city guard's wages exercises real influence in Tidecrest — acknowledged quietly by everyone who actually has to get business done there.
Day-to-day administration in Tidecrest runs through tax-farmers who keep a cut of everything they collect, a system that works well enough in ordinary times but strains badly under any real crisis.

sections.title: Tension
paragraphs: Tidecrest's deepest ongoing friction is over a border shrine both sides claim, a dispute that shapes local politics more than any formal law does.
Tension in Tidecrest currently sits at a simmer — real, openly discussed, but not yet at open conflict.
The root of Tidecrest's trouble is a border shrine both sides claim, a dispute old enough that most residents have simply learned to live around it.
Tidecrest rarely sees real violence over this, but trade disputes have been known to bring things close to a boil, especially during the busy trading season.

sections.title: History
paragraphs: Tidecrest was settled by Undine migrants and grew into its current standing as a village on the strength of its trade in salt, which remains the backbone of its economy today.
Tidecrest was founded by early Undine settlers of Tidewrought Commonwealth, drawn to the site by exactly the resources that still support the city's trade.
In its history, Tidecrest grew rich off a single trade good before diversifying, an event still referenced in local memory and civic ritual.
As a result, its old founding families still hold outsized influence, a legacy every resident of Tidecrest would recognize immediately even if outsiders rarely do.

trade_routes.sought_as: a staple Ashgate Reach cannot produce enough of on its own
trade_routes.acquisition: Merchant convoys load grain at Brackgate's market yards, bought up from the Ardenhale producers who supply it, then carry it overland or by ship toward Drossakar.
trade_routes.demand: Ashwatch and the wider Ashgate Reach market cannot produce grain locally in any quantity, so imported supply from Brackgate covers a real, recurring shortfall rather than a luxury want.
trade_routes.conduct: The exchange runs through licensed factors on both ends — Brackgate's export houses and Ashwatch's import brokers — who settle accounts in coin or barter goods each trading season rather than per shipment.
trade_routes.friction: The route crosses from Kelmoria to Drossakar, so it is exposed to weather, piracy, and the ordinary toll disputes of whichever ports and nations it passes through, and either side's local political trouble can stall a season's shipments.

races.name: Goblin
body: Small, wiry, sharp-toothed, disproportionately strong for their size.
senses: They see in pitch darkness as well as in daylight.
races.about: Goblin trace their homeland to drossakar's warrens, ash-fields, and salvage-middens, and even where they've spread across Aurvantis, that origin still shapes their architecture, diet, and holidays. Sprawling, loosely bounded clan-swarms with fluid membership. Goblin livelihoods are shaped directly by Drossakar's ash-fields, iron-rich badlands, geothermal vents, and their traditional trades reflect exactly what that land offers. Goblin craft goods are recognizable across Aurvantis by their distinctive materials and style, and command a premium in foreign markets specifically because of that origin.

races.name: Half-Orc
body: Human build with orcish ruggedness — a heavier brow, sometimes visible tusks.
senses: They see in pitch darkness as well as in daylight.
races.about: Half-Orc trace their homeland to border towns between drossakar's clans and its human-settled fringes, and even where they've spread across Aurvantis, that origin still shapes their architecture, diet, and holidays. Found-family and chosen-crew loyalty, born of frequent estrangement from both parent cultures. Half-Orc livelihoods are shaped directly by Drossakar's ash-fields, iron-rich badlands, geothermal vents, and their traditional trades reflect exactly what that land offers. Half-Orc craft goods are recognizable across Aurvantis by their distinctive materials and style, and command a premium in foreign markets specifically because of that origin.

races.name: Hobgoblin
body: Disciplined, compact builds, red-to-orange skin tones, notably uniform posture and bearing.
senses: They see in pitch darkness as well as in daylight.
races.about: Hobgoblin trace their homeland to drossakar's fortress-cities and militarized frontier, and even where they've spread across Aurvantis, that origin still shapes their architecture, diet, and holidays. Military-unit loyalty frequently supersedes family loyalty entirely. Hobgoblin livelihoods are shaped directly by Drossakar's ash-fields, iron-rich badlands, geothermal vents, and their traditional trades reflect exactly what that land offers. Hobgoblin craft goods are recognizable across Aurvantis by their distinctive materials and style, and command a premium in foreign markets specifically because of that origin.

races.name: Orc
body: Powerfully built, prominent lower tusks, thick hide that resists minor scarring.
senses: They see in pitch darkness as well as in daylight.
races.about: Orc trace their homeland to volcanic badlands and iron ranges of drossakar, and even where they've spread across Aurvantis, that origin still shapes their architecture, diet, and holidays. Warband loyalty often outweighs blood ties. Orc livelihoods are shaped directly by Drossakar's ash-fields, iron-rich badlands, geothermal vents, and their traditional trades reflect exactly what that land offers. Orc craft goods are recognizable across Aurvantis by their distinctive materials and style, and command a premium in foreign markets specifically because of that origin.

races.name: Elf
body: Tall, slender, faintly angular features, low body fat even in cold climates.
senses: They see clearly by dusk light and keep working in it.
Acute hearing.
races.about: Elf trace their homeland to old-growth forest, tended more than owned, and even where they've spread across Aurvantis, that origin still shapes their architecture, diet, and holidays. Multi-generational households where the eldest living member holds final say. Elf livelihoods are shaped directly by Kelmoria's river-valley farmland, old-growth deciduous forest, rolling downs, and their traditional trades reflect exactly what that land offers. Elf craft goods are recognizable across Aurvantis by their distinctive materials and style, and command a premium in foreign markets specifically because of that origin.

races.name: Gnome
body: Small, wiry, skin and hair that can shift hue with mood over months, not moments.
senses: They see clearly by dusk light and keep working in it.
Unusually keen sense of smell.
races.about: Gnome trace their homeland to wherever the last interesting thing happened; famously restless, and even where they've spread across Aurvantis, that origin still shapes their architecture, diet, and holidays. Loose clan ties; personal reputation for cleverness matters more than lineage. Gnome livelihoods are shaped directly by Kelmoria's river-valley farmland, old-growth deciduous forest, rolling downs, and their traditional trades reflect exactly what that land offers. Gnome craft goods are recognizable across Aurvantis by their distinctive materials and style, and command a premium in foreign markets specifically because of that origin.

races.name: Half-Elf
body: Human build with subtler elven features; varies individual to individual.
senses: They see clearly by dusk light and keep working in it.
races.about: Half-Elf trace their homeland to border regions where human and elf settlement overlap, and even where they've spread across Aurvantis, that origin still shapes their architecture, diet, and holidays. Often builds found-family networks outside strict bloodline reckoning. Half-Elf livelihoods are shaped directly by Kelmoria's river-valley farmland, old-growth deciduous forest, rolling downs, and their traditional trades reflect exactly what that land offers. Half-Elf craft goods are recognizable across Aurvantis by their distinctive materials and style, and command a premium in foreign markets specifically because of that origin.

races.name: Human
body: Physically unremarkable and highly variable; adapts to any climate within a generation or two.
senses: Ordinary five senses.
races.about: Human trace their homeland to no single homeland; the most adaptable and widespread people on aurvantis, and even where they've spread across Aurvantis, that origin still shapes their architecture, diet, and holidays. Extended family and marriage-alliance networks dominate inheritance and politics. Human livelihoods are shaped directly by Kelmoria's river-valley farmland, old-growth deciduous forest, rolling downs, and their traditional trades reflect exactly what that land offers. Human craft goods are recognizable across Aurvantis by their distinctive materials and style, and command a premium in foreign markets specifically because of that origin.

races.name: Dwarf

senses: They see in pitch darkness as well as in daylight.

Dwarf livelihoods are shaped directly by Sunkeep Reaches's high desert plateau, undercliff cave networks, scattered oases, and their traditional trades reflect exactly what that land offers. Dwarf craft goods are recognizable across Aurvantis by their distinctive materials and style, and command a premium in foreign markets specifically because of that origin.

Extended caravan-families that may not share blood but share the road. Halfling livelihoods are shaped directly by Sunkeep Reaches's high desert plateau, undercliff cave networks, scattered oases, and their traditional trades reflect exactly what that land offers. Halfling craft goods are recognizable across Aurvantis by their distinctive materials and style, and command a premium in foreign markets specifically because of that origin.

races.name: Undine
body: Human-adjacent build with faintly blue-toned skin and a permanent, subtle scent of the sea.
senses: Can hold breath far longer than a human, sees clearly underwater.
races.about: Undine trace their homeland to veyl isles' tidal flats and coral cities, and even where they've spread across Aurvantis, that origin still shapes their architecture, diet, and holidays. Tide-bound communal households, membership shifting with the season's fishing grounds. Undine livelihoods are shaped directly by Veyl Isles's coral reef shallows, mangrove wetland, high island canopy forest, and their traditional trades reflect exactly what that land offers. Undine craft goods are recognizable across Aurvantis by their distinctive materials and style, and command a premium in foreign markets specifically because of that origin.

races.name: Vanara
body: Simian features, a fully prehensile tail.
senses: They see clearly by dusk light and keep working in it.
races.about: Vanara trace their homeland to veyl isles' canopy settlements, built high in the island forests, and even where they've spread across Aurvantis, that origin still shapes their architecture, diet, and holidays. Canopy-councils led by the troop's most respected elders remains this faction's chief opponent, treating it as a persistent irritant rather than an existential threat — a judgment that may not age well.

cards.title: A faction within Mireflote Concord actively contests a disputed succession
facts: A faction within Mireflote Concord actively contests a disputed succession, organizing support in whichever of the nation's cities gives it the most leverage.

Its influence is concentrated in one or two of Mireflote Concord's four cities rather than spread evenly across the nation, which is exactly why the formal government has been slow to move against it.

timeline.name: The Salt Fever
timeline.summary: A wasting sickness swept coastal populations on three continents; its cure — a Veyl Isles undine remedy — remains the basis of Aurvantis's most-traded medicine.

timeline.name: Present Day
timeline.summary: The Long Peace Accords still formally hold, strained but unbroken, as four continents' nations trade, feud, and expand into the current era.
